seoDescription: Learn how to generate and implement custom icons and splash screens in your Ionic 7 and Capacitor 5 applications. This guide covers using the latest Capacitor splash screen and icon package, including preparing resource files with the correct dimensions for Android, iOS, and PWA. It addresses common issues and workarounds for Android 12 and 12L splash screen visibility, details capacitor.config.ts settings, and demonstrates how to test and verify your assets on both platforms for a professional app launch experience.

chapters.title: Initial Setup & Asset Preparation
chapters.description: Learn how to install the Capacitor assets package and prepare the five required source images (icon, foreground, background, splash, splash-dark) in a 'resources' folder with the correct dimensions.

chapters.title: Generating Icons & Splash Screens
chapters.description: Run the 'npx capacitor-assets generate' command after adding platforms to automatically create all platform-specific icon and splash screen files for Android, iOS, and PWA.

chapters.title: Understanding Android 12+ Splash Screen Behavior
chapters.description: Explore the specific behavior of splash screens on Android 12+ and learn about an unresolved issue with third-party launchers noted by the Capacitor team.

chapters.title: Configuring Splash Screen Options
chapters.description: Configure splash screen settings like duration and background color in the 'capacitor.config.ts' file and review required CSS styles.

chapters.title: Testing on Android
chapters.description: Sync your project, open it in Android Studio, and run it on an Android 13 emulator to verify that the custom icon and splash screen are working correctly.

chapters.title: Testing on iOS
chapters.description: Open the project in Xcode, run it on an iOS simulator, and confirm that the generated icon and splash screen display as expected on the iOS platform.

chapters.title: Workaround for Android 12 Splash Screen Issue
chapters.description: Demonstrates a practical workaround for the Android 12/12L splash screen issue by closing the app and relaunching it from the device's app launcher.

chapters.title: Fixing iOS Splash Screen Sizing
chapters.description: Use an online tool called Image Gorilla to regenerate correctly sized splash screen assets for iOS and manually replace them in the Xcode project to fix display issues.

chapters.title: Final Verification & Conclusion
chapters.description: Perform a final check on the iOS simulator to confirm the sizing fix and review the key takeaways from implementing custom assets in Ionic 7 with Capacitor 5.

summary:
## Generating Custom Assets with Capacitor 5

- **Tool**: `@capacitor/assets` package.
- **Installation**: `npm install @capacitor/assets`
- **Generation Command**: `npx capacitor-assets generate`

## Required Source Images

Create a `resources` folder in your project root and add the following 5 source images:

- `icon-only.png` (1024x1024): Used for legacy icons and PWAs.
- `icon-foreground.png` (1024x1024): The foreground layer for Android adaptive icons.
- `icon.png` (1024x1024): The background layer for Android adaptive icons.
- `splash.png` (2732x2732): Splash screen for light mode.
- `splash-dark.png` (2732x2732): Splash screen for dark mode.

> [!TIP]
> The video demonstrates using the same image file for all three icon variations by renaming it, which is a quick way to get started.

## Key Commands Workflow

1.  `ionic build`: Creates the web asset `www` folder. This is a prerequisite.
2.  `ionic cap add android` / `ionic cap add ios`: Adds the native platforms to your project.
3.  `npx capacitor-assets generate`: Generates all necessary icon and splash screen files for the added platforms.
4.  `ionic cap sync`: Copies web assets and updates the native projects with the new configurations.
5.  `ionic cap open android` / `ionic cap open ios`: Opens the native project in Android Studio or Xcode for testing.

## Splash Screen Configuration

Configure splash screen behavior in `capacitor.config.ts` under the `splashScreen` plugin key.

**Example Settings:**
```typescript
{
  "plugins": {
    "SplashScreen": {
      "launchShowDuration": 2000,
      "backgroundColor": "#ffffffff",
      "showSpinner": false,
      "splashFullScreen": true,
      "splashImmersive": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Platform-Specific Issues & Solutions

### Android 12 / 12L Splash Screen

> [!IMPORTANT]
> By default, the splash screen may appear as a blank white screen on Android 12/12L when launching from an IDE like Android Studio. This is a known OS-level issue related to third-party launchers that Google has not backported a fix for.

**Workaround**:

1.  Launch the app from the IDE (splash screen may be blank).
2.  Close the app completely from the device's recent apps stack.
3.  Re-launch the app by tapping its icon from the device's home screen or app drawer. The splash screen should now appear correctly.

### iOS Splash Screen Sizing

> [!NOTE]
> If the automatically generated splash screen appears zoomed or incorrectly sized on iOS devices, you may need to regenerate and manually replace the assets.

**Solution**:

1.  Use a service like **Image Gorilla** to generate new iOS-specific splash screen assets from your source `splash.png`.
2.  In Xcode, open the project and navigate to `App > App > Assets.xcassets > Splash`.
3.  Manually drag and drop the newly generated image files into the `1x`, `2x`, and `3x` slots in the Image Set for both "Any Appearance" and "Dark Appearance".
4.  Re-run the app from Xcode to verify the correct sizing.
